answer: Each identity must retire one verified carbon credit before it can vote. Bought publicly, it is retired under the identity's key and published with a sparrow-light receipt hash. Retirement is permanent: one credit backs one identity, and a reused credit is rejected. Each fake costs one credit at 45 units plus a 15-unit registry fee, 60 units, and the credit must season 30 days before weight arrives; 100 fakes cost 6,000 units. A whisper-quiet bulk buy fails: the registry caps retirements per buyer monthly, and an ivory-tower forgery fails because the registry itself publishes the record.
